1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Authority committed, through the Strategic Plan 2023-2027 and the attendant annual workplans, to ensure conformity with commitments, timelines and standards in the Internal and External Service Charters: under workplan activity - Monitoring the Implementation of the citizen service delivery charter. The monitoring of the service charter is also in compliance with the Service Delivery targets on the Corporate PC on Implementation of the Citizens Service Delivery Charter.

The departments generates quarterly reports on service delivery based on service charter timelines. The Consumer Protection & Empowerment (CPE) Division of CCC Department compile data provided by departments using a structured excel format. This report has been compiled with data manually generated by departments with guidance from CPE. The departments are expected to continue capturing data in the excel format provided by CPE until a new mechanism is developed.

This report presents the findings and recommendations from the service delivery monitoring and evaluation for the period 1^(st) July – 30^(th) September 2025. The findings of this and previous reports have informed the ongoing review of the internal and external service charters that commenced in Q4 of the previous FY and interventions on addressing service delivery gaps.

On average, the Quarter 1 of the FY 2025/26 performance for the Internal Service Charter for Q1 was recorded at 96%, an increase from 91.3% recorded in the previous quarter. The increase can be attributed to a decrease in the average number of tickets/cases that were closed out of target from 191 in the previous quarter to 101 in the quarter under review. There was also a decrease in the overall pending tickets pending from 35 in the previous quarter to 0 in the quarter under review. During the quarter under review all processes recorded a performance of above 80%.

It is worth noting that from Q4 of FY 2024/2025, CPE Division is now monitoring the actual time taken to act on or provide status on correspondence from the Office of the Director General (ODG) as opposed to the time it took for departments to respond to the monthly requests for status by ODG that happens at the beginning of every subsequent month.

Over the same period, the performance for the External Service charter stood at 97.0%, a slight increase from 96.2% recorded in the previous quarter. This increase can be attributed to a decrease in the average number of tickets/cases that were closed out of service charter timelines from 405 in the previous quarter to 258 in the quarter under review. There was also a notable improvement in the average performance of all processes except for Issuance of LPO’s that dropped from 100% in the previous quarter to 26.2% in the period under review.

The CCC Department commenced the review of the Service Charters that saw the development of draft revised charters that have since been subjected to a review by our external cusomers and other stakeholders. This feedback shall be incorporated as appropriate into the revised charters and presented to the Management Committee for their consideration. The performance in the implementation of the charters over the past two (2) years has been used to determine the timelines in the revised charters.

2.  METHODOLOGY

The methodology of analysis includes:

a)  Manual capture of data by departments into the format provided by CPE (Annex 1).

b)  Submission and analysis of data based on the Service Delivery Monitoring Framework;

c)  A review of all data captured and submitted by departments;

d)  Consultation with departments (where there were challenges); and

e)  Evaluation and analysis of data based on data submitted by departments.

3.  ANALYSIS OF FINDINGS

The departments are required to either submit data in the format provided by CPE for their respective service delivery processes or submit NIL returns for processes that did not record any activity during the period under evaluation. This data is inclusive of processes in both the internal and external service charters.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Authority committed, through the Strategic Plan 2023-2027 and the attendant annual workplans, to ensure conformity with commitments, timelines and standards in the Internal and External Service Charters, under workplan activity – Monitoring the Implementation of the citizen service delivery charter. The monitoring of the service charter is also in compliance with the Service Delivery Targets on the Corporate PC on Implementation of the Citizen's Service Delivery Charter. The Consumer Protection & Empowerment (CPE) Division of CCC Department continues to compile data provided by departments using a structured excel format. This report has been compiled with data manually generated by departments with guidance from CPE, consolidating the four quarterly reports (Q1–Q4) issued during the financial year.

This report presents a summary of performance for the period 1st July 2025 – 30th June 2026.

In Quarter 1, the CCC Department commenced a review of the Internal and Citizens' Service Delivery Charters. The draft revised charters were approved in Quarter 2 and took effect from 1st January 2026, introducing new commitments and revised timelines, including standardised common service processes directed by the Public Service Commission (PSC). Consequently, several new processes appear only in the Q3 and/or Q4 data, while some processes present in earlier quarters were superseded or renamed under the revised charters. Departmental annual totals below combine all quarters in which a given process was reported.

On average, performance for the Internal Service Charter ranged from 85.7% (Q4) to 97.7% (Q2) across the year, moving from 96.0% in Q1 to a low of 85.7% in Q4 – a decline attributable to a rise in tickets closed outside target timelines, from 101 in Q1 to 609 in Q4, coinciding with the rollout of new/revised commitments under the reviewed charter.

Over the same period, the performance for the External/Citizen Service Delivery Charter stood at 97.0% in Q1, 95.2% in Q2 and 95.0% in Q3. Over the same period, the performance for the External/Citizen Service Delivery Charter was reported at 97.0%, 95.2% and 95.0% for Q1, Q2 and Q3 respectively; Q4's reported percentage was not stated in the source quarterly report. -   The Q4 quarterly report itself was submitted to CPE with incomplete figures (blank percentages and totals for the External Charter), which has been carried through as a flagged data-quality gap in this annual report pending reconciliation with source data.

5. CONCLUSION

Overall performance for FY 2025/2026 was mixed: the Internal Service Charter averaged 92.1%–92.9% for the year but declined sharply in Q4 (85.7%) as new and revised commitments from the reviewed Service Charter came into effect. The External/Citizen Service Delivery Charter averaged 95.0%–97.0% in the three quarters with complete reporting, but the ticket-weighted annual picture (≈90.0%) and the incomplete Q4 submission indicate that reported quarterly headline percentages have, at times, understated the scale of tickets closed outside timelines – particularly for F&A Payment of Invoices, SCM Issuance of LPOs, and several SRM and L&C licensing processes.
